chunks: From him, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Khalid ibn Najih, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about stomach pain, so he said to me: 'Take the rice, wash it, then dry it in the shade, then powder it, and take from it every morning an amount that fits in the palm of your hand.' And Is'haq al-Jariri added: 'Fry it slightly, the weight of one Awqiya, and drink it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the traditional Shia remedy for stomach pain mentioned in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the integration of prophetic medicine (*al-Tibb al-Nabawi*) with the Imams' practical guidance, emphasizing the therapeutic use of rice (*al-Aruz*) for gastrointestinal ailments. The specific preparation method—washing, shade-drying, and powdering—reflects a nuanced understanding of food properties in Shia medical tradition, while the addition of light frying (*taqlih*) by Is-haq al-Jariri highlights the transmission of refined culinary-medical practices. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how daily sustenance was viewed as a means of healing within the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings.

en.hubeali: From him, from Usman Bin Isa, from Khalid Bin Najeeh who said,

‘I complained to Abu Abdullahasws of stomach pains, so heasws said to me: ‘Take the rice, wash it, then dry it in the shade, then powder it, and take from it during every morning as per your convenience’. And Is’haq Al Jareery increased in it, ‘(Heasws said): ‘Fry it a little, the weight of one Awqiya (Unit of measurement), and drink it’.
en.sarwar: 6. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Khalid ibn Najih who has said the following:

“I once complained before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about pain in my belly. He (the Imam) said, ‘Take rice, wash it, then dry it in the shadow, crush it; then take one fill of your palm every morning.’ Ishaq al-Jaririy has added that it should be fried a little and taken one awqiyah to drink.”
